elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New 16.7: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — the cap runs against both Array and Ono; computing the amount off sums payable by Ono does not make it one-sided (it mirrors the model "fees paid by Customer" basis).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 16.7 caps at "the fees and other amounts payable by Ono ... during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" with no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor and no "paid or payable" formulation.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 16.5: "IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY ... BE LIABLE ... FOR SPECIAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, INCIDENTAL OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES SUFFERED BY THE OTHER PARTY" — mutual and left untouched.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 carve-out: "either Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article X (Confidentiality)"; the caption at p0520 confirms Article X is the confidentiality article and the carve-out is drafted functionally so it does not hinge on the cross-reference.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 lists only indemnification (16.1/16.2), confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security carve-out.

16.7 carves out only "indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2". Retained 16.5 expressly recognises "THE INDEMNITIES PROVIDED PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 10, SECTIONS 16.1 AND 16.2", so indemnities arising under Article 10 remain inside the new cap.
16.7 excepts "either Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct".
16.7 excepts "either Party's gross negligence or willful misconduct".
No fraud carve-out appears in 16.7 or elsewhere in the rendered language.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7 contains no carve-out for infringement of the other Party's intellectual property rights.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Nothing in 16.7 states that Ono's payment obligations (milestones, royalties, fees) are not "damages" subject to the cap; on its face the cap could be read to limit recovery of amounts owed.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 16.7 applies to "each Party's total aggregate liability", so Array and Ono are both capped; no residual unlimited-Customer language.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 16.7: "the fees and other amounts payable by Ono under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee-based basis.

The carve-out is limited to Sections 16.1 and 16.2; retained 16.5 shows the Agreement also contains indemnities "PURSUANT TO ARTICLE 10", which the new 16.7 leaves subject to the cap. Not all indemnification obligations are uncapped.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 16.7: "either Party's breach of its confidentiality obligations under Article X (Confidentiality)" — functionally drafted and mutual.

reasons: Fallback is one element short: the indemnification carve-out in new 16.7 is drafted narrowly as "indemnification obligations under Sections 16.1 and 16.2", but retained 16.5 expressly identifies indemnities under Article 10 as well. Repair the operative text to read "each Party's indemnification obligations under this Agreement (including under Article 10 and Sections 16.1 and 16.2)" so no indemnity source remains inside the cap.

Related consistency point: as drafted, 16.7 subjects Article 10 third-party indemnity payments to a 12-month cap even though 16.5 preserves those amounts from the consequential-damages waiver; the broadened carve-out above cures this tension as well.

Preferred level is correctly not claimed: no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor, no "paid or payable" basis, and no carve-outs for data protection/security, fraud or infringement of the other Party's IP, and no statement that Ono's payment obligations are outside the cap.

Minimality holds: a single concise new Section 16.7 is inserted to fill a genuinely missing cap, 16.5 and all other language are left untouched, and no survival tail, expense language, procedure or extra damages category is added.

Intent is preserved: 16.5's mutual consequential-damages waiver and its indemnity/gross-negligence provisos survive unchanged, the Article X cross-reference resolves to the confidentiality article, and no term is left dangling or undefined.
